candidates.attacker_control: A user able to configure a SecureGroovyScript classpath entry can supply an arbitrary URL, including an HTTP(S) URL they control. They control the response bytes independently for the approval/runtime hash requests and the subsequent class-loader request. They also control the script that references a class from that JAR.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The code does rehash the entry in ScriptApproval.using immediately before constructing the URLClassLoader, which narrows the window but does not make the check and use refer to the same bytes. No signature verification or local materialization is present. URLConnection or URLClassLoader caching could reduce exploitability for some deployments, and approval of an attacker-supplied remote URL may already be viewed as administrator trust; however, the hash-based approval model implies content binding, so substituting content after approval violates the intended control.
candidates.impact: A mutable classpath entry can escape the content-approval control and execute attacker-controlled code in the Jenkins controller JVM, potentially bypassing the Groovy sandbox and leading to full controller compromise.
candidates.prerequisites: An integrating plugin must expose SecureGroovyScript classpath configuration to a lower-privileged user. A Jenkins administrator must approve the benign classpath content hash in the normal approval workflow. The attacker must be able to serve different content from the same URL and have the malicious JAR expose a member marked @Whitelisted, or otherwise invoke an approved classpath entry through a sandboxed script.
candidates.root_cause: Classpath approval is content-addressed, but the approved hash is not bound to the bytes later loaded. ScriptApproval.using hashes the URL by opening it, then SecureGroovyScript.evaluate independently adds the same URL to a URLClassLoader without pinning verified bytes or rechecking the loaded JAR. An attacker controlling a remote classpath URL can serve approved bytes for the hash read and different bytes for the later class-load request.
candidates.title: Classpath content-hash approval can be bypassed by changing URL content between hashing and class loading
candidates.trace: ScriptApproval.configuring(ClasspathEntry, ApprovalContext) calls checkAndConvertApprovedClasspath, which reads the URL via Hasher.hashClasspathEntry and records or approves only the hash. At evaluation, ScriptApproval.using(entry) performs another hash read and succeeds if served bytes match the approved hash. Immediately afterward, SecureGroovyScript.evaluate places the original URL in ClasspathURLClassLoader/URLClassLoader and class loading opens the URL again. Nothing ties those later bytes to the hash-verified stream, so a different JAR can be loaded. AnnotatedWhitelist permits any method, constructor, or field carrying @Whitelisted regardless of which classloader defined the JAR; a script can invoke the swapped-in @Whitelisted code.
candidates.unverified: No runtime test or exploit was executed. The exact URLClassLoader behavior for remote JAR URLs, request caching, and whether a given integrating plugin exposes classpath configuration to the attacker were not verified. The malicious JAR's @Whitelisted method invocation was inferred from source, not observed.

coverage_summary: Accounted for all 49 controller-visible files. Inspected the principal sandbox and approval paths: GroovySandbox, SandboxInterceptor, GroovyCallSiteSelector, ClassLoaderWhitelist, SandboxResolvingClassLoader, RejectASTTransformsCustomizer, SecureGroovyScript, ScriptApproval, ClasspathEntry, and the whitelist implementations. Tests, dependency sources, compiled artifacts, and default whitelist/blacklist resource files are not in the visible snapshot.
limitations: No code was executed and no exploit or runtime behavior was tested.
The default whitelist and blacklist resources, tests, Groovy/groovy-sandbox dependency source, and Jenkins UI/Jelly/Stapler framework behavior are outside the visible snapshot.
Exploitability depends on an integrating plugin exposing classpath configuration to a lower-privileged user and an administrator approving a mutable remote URL or content.
Remote JAR handling and URL caching by the JDK URLClassLoader were not verified in this environment.
The repository snapshot is reduced to 49 files and does not establish the complete set of consuming plugins or all approved signatures.

rejected_leads.lead: Sandbox call-site selector may choose a different overload than Groovy, allowing a whitelisted signature to authorize an unwhitelisted method.
rejected_leads.reason: GroovyCallSiteSelector has acknowledged incomplete Java/Groovy overload emulation, but no concrete pair of a whitelisted overload and a distinct dangerous runtime-dispatched overload was established from the visible source and whitelist data.

rejected_leads.lead: The AST-transform blocklist may be incomplete, yielding a compile-time or runtime sandbox bypass.
rejected_leads.reason: The blocklist only names selected transforms, but no specific omitted transform was traced to an executable dangerous path with available classes and sandbox-instrumentation gaps in this snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: Generated Groovy invokeMethod or getMetaClass methods from script-defined classes may allow reflective dispatch around interception.
rejected_leads.reason: ClassLoaderWhitelist permits non-synthetic members of script-defined classes, but whether generated dispatch bypasses interception for an unwhitelisted inherited method was not demonstrated from source alone.

rejected_leads.lead: State-changing ScriptApproval JavaScript methods lack explicit RequirePOST annotations and may be CSRF-able.
rejected_leads.reason: All relevant methods check Jenkins.ADMINISTER; the effective Stapler JavaScript-method HTTP requirements are provided by framework code not present in this snapshot.

summary: Reviewed the visible Script Security snapshot, focusing on sandbox interception, call-site selection, approval hashing, classpath approval, and whitelist trust. The strongest source-evidenced lead is a classpath hash TOCTOU: approval hashes URL bytes in one read, but evaluation later opens the same mutable URL with a URLClassLoader, so the approved hash need not bind the JAR actually loaded. A class in a swapped JAR can carry @Whitelisted members, which AnnotatedWhitelist accepts without a plugin/classloader trust check. This is a lead, not runtime-confirmed.
